Plot how much memory one pathway needs

Source: R/plot_diagnostics.R
plot_pruning.Rd

plot_pruning() plots how much memory one pathway needs: how many past states are needed to predict what follows it. A context tree keeps a longer history only when it predicts the next state differently from its shorter suffix, and the plot makes that decision visible for one pathway. It follows the pathway's suffix chain (the full history, then the history without its earliest state, and so on down to the root) and draws the next-state distribution at every link as its own panel, deepest history on the left and the root on the right.

Each context is classified by the \(G^2\) rule of prune_tree(): the likelihood-ratio statistic of its next-state counts against its one-shorter parent is compared with the chi-square critical value at alpha. A context whose own \(G^2\) exceeds it adds memory and is drawn solid; a context below it that is kept only because a deeper context exceeds it is drawn at medium opacity; a context below it with no deeper context exceeding it is pruned and drawn faded. Each panel title gives the context, the decision and \(G^2\). The distributions are the node values reported by tree_pathways() and query_pathway().

Pass an unpruned tree so that the whole chain is visible. To prune the whole tree use prune_tree(); to compare pruning rules use compare_pruning().

Usage

plot_pruning(tree, pathway, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object, usually unpruned.

pathway

One fitted context in arrow notation ("A -> B -> C", earliest state on the left).

alpha

Significance level of the \(G^2\) test. Default 0.05.

Value

A ggplot object with one panel per context of the suffix chain.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input

(error) tree is not a transitiontrees object; alpha is not in (0, 1); pathway is not a context of the tree.

See also

prune_tree(), compare_pruning(), plot_distributions().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
plot_pruning(tree, "Average -> Active -> Active")
